member.name: ReconcileSequenceAsync
member.para: The book that lost a chapter to a hallucinated duplicate. "Atlan" (build 392, 2026-08-24), 14:19:43, German, run with -fs. One 30 s probe window at 2:28:17.79 came back with two segments and both matched the chapter phrase: "Kapitel 5" at 0.0-12.0 (p=0.58) and "Kapitel 6" at 12.0-40.0 (p=0.60). The second is a recognizer artefact - its timestamps run ten seconds past the end of the window they were decoded from, and every other read of that audio (three survival probes, seven onset probes, a 45 s re-read, the gap transcription) hears one announcement followed by "Auserhalb des von Einstein definierten Raumzeitkontinuums…" - but both matches anchored to the same jingle-end silence at 2:28:25.44, so both refined to the same onset and both were marked at 2:28:25.26.

The refinement vote read the phantom correctly: "refinement read chapter 6 at 2:28:29.79 as 5 (3 of 3 readings), outside the sequence after chapter 5 - keeping 6". Three of three, and refused, because 5 does not continue a sequence that had accepted chapter 5 one second earlier at that same position. That is the guard exception added here.

What the phantom then cost. The real chapter 6 at 2:47:23 was found three times and discarded three times. Probe read it twice ("Kapitel 6" at 2:47:15.80, plain and on the one-pass re-read) and skipped both as "not above last accepted 6". Re-probe placed it properly at 2:47:23.42 with p=0.77 - and , having to choose between two marks numbered 6, kept the earlier one. Scan then transcribed the region and heard it a third time (gap chunk from 2:38:15.26, segment at 548.1 s = 2:47:23.4, p=0.78), where the "already a known chapter" guard dropped it without a log line. The collision was settled correctly at the very end - re-read at 2:28:23.61, "Kapitel 5", phantom removed - by which point the book's only remaining chapter 6 had been thrown away twice, so it ended with none.

And the display could not say so. The status line read "(-1)" for the whole 45-minute run: counts the numbers a sequence holds, and the phantom held 6, so only 7 was ever missing. The collision settle that removed it ran after the last progress refresh, so even the final reading was the one taken while the sequence was still wrong. Both halves of that are fixed here; the file's own ".missing-marks-6-7" tag was correct throughout, being recomputed from the finished sequence.

Chapter 7 is a separate matter and not this defect: no "Kapitel 7" appears in any transcript of the run, over a region transcribed twice at different framings plus 75 sub-floor pauses probed, and the jingle census finds no music at all between 2:47:06 and 4:11:41 while all 33 detected chapters of the book begin at music.

member.name: DropNamedMarkEchoes
member.para: The epilogue heading that became a chapter. "Corsa nello spazio" (build 251, 2026-08-06), whose epilogue is headed "Epilogo / 2179 / Spazio profondo". Under --chapter-phrase none a year spoken alone is an announcement by definition, and a well-formed one - set off by real pauses, read as 2179 by every probe that saw it - so it reached the written file as "Capitolo 2179", 2.86 s after the epilogue's own mark. It also pushed the sequence ceiling to 2179, which declared chapters 66-2178 missing and cost about 25 minutes of a 90-minute run hunting through empty audio.

member.name: RepairSequenceOutliersAsync
member.para: The worked example. "Die Cyber-Brutzellen" (2026-08-01): the announcement at 7:01:30 was read as chapter 40, sits between chapter 13 at 6:21:09 and chapter 15 at 7:47:34, and 14 is therefore the only number it can carry. Neither bounding chapter was known when the misreading happened - 15 had been found but not yet related to it, and everything up to 29 came later.
What the repair saves downstream. On that same file, 14 minutes spent searching the stretch between 6:21 and 7:01 for a chapter 14 whose announcement sits at the far end of it.

member.name: RescanShiftedAsync
member.para: The chapter that vanished from a full transcription. Chapter 14 of "Paula Monti" (2026-07-31) is the case on record and the measurement behind the shift: decoded from 2:30:31.29 the 601 s chunk produced "…solennité dramatique." / "Berthe de Brevan occupait une des places de cette loge." with "Première partie, chapitre 14, première loge numéro 7" simply absent between them, reproducibly at every chunk length tried from 120 s to 601 s. The identical chunk decoded from 2:30:46.29 - the same audio, 15 s later - reads it at p=0.94.

End to end on that clip (-m turbo, which switches Re-probe off so the case reaches Scan at all): Scan recovered chapter 13 from the head of the gap and left 14 missing exactly as before, and the shifted re-read placed it at the same mark the Re-probe sweep produces, 0.93 confidence.

member.name: SweepSubFloorSilencesAsync
member.para: The book whose breaks all landed on the floor. "Paula Monti" (2026-07-31, French, 4 h 34 min): all five chapters Probe missed were preceded by a pause of 1.39-1.49 s against a 1.5 s floor. Four were eventually recovered by Scan transcribing whole gaps, and the fifth was lost outright because Whisper's long-form decode swallowed the announcement - a 601 s chunk produced a contiguous transcript with the words "Première partie, chapitre 14, première loge numéro 7" simply absent from it, reproducibly, while any short window aimed at the same audio read them cleanly.

What the sweeps came to on the same file, re-run 2026-07-31 with them in place: all five gaps closed here, one probe each (two candidates only for chapter 19's band), Scan never ran at all, and the run transcribed 1:00:43 of audio instead of 1:49:57 - 45 % less - while finding two chapters more than before. Chapters 3, 12 and 16 came back on the exact marks Scan's full transcription had produced.

member.name: SweepAdaptiveSubFloorAsync
member.para: What a wider candidate list did instead. The obvious implementation - have Analyze keep everything down to and let the threshold admit what it likes - was built first and measured on a 25-minute BARDIOC clip (2026-08-08, build 257): going from 27 candidates to 200 re-cut the last two minutes from 49.4 s and 34.9 s decodes into 28.8, 19.8 and 13.5 s, and chapter 2's announcement at 0:24:44.73 - heard comfortably by the long decode - fell 1.2 s short of the end of a short one and was lost, along with the jingle re-read that inherits that end. The candidate list is the grid the windows are planned on, so extra entries re-cut the decodes of the whole book.

The break length that would make an ungated sweep unbounded. "Die Dritte Macht" (2026-07-28) measures a 0.54 s break, so without the gap gate and the budget it would sweep the whole sub-floor range across its whole fifteen hours - thousands of probes for pauses no chapter is missing behind.
